record_type_quote: In this paper we present a replication study of the first inoculation experiment conducted by McGuire and Papageorgis (1961), who introduced inoculation theory.

targets.title: The relative efficacy of various types of prior belief-defense in producing immunity against persuasion.
targets.evidence_quote: In this paper we present a replication study of the first inoculation experiment conducted by McGuire and Papageorgis (1961), who introduced inoculation theory.
targets.outcome_quote: The results demonstrate a (for the most part) successful replication. When grouping the truisms, we find the same pattern of results as in the original study. The inoculation treatment resulted in more resistance than the supportive treatment and the control condition, confirming H1 and H2.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly judge the replication as a whole successful, with qualification, and conclude on the basis of a successful replication. This overall verdict governs despite the separately discussed failure of H2 on one topic; reduced effect size alone does not make mixed.

reasoning: Publisher DOI and repository full article title and all authors match. Completed registered report with results; one original paper. Main comparisons pooled across the truisms replicate both hypotheses. Bibliography identifies the 1961 article, not the 1964/1981 theoretical chapter or later applications.
